title: HB952 (2023 Regular): Crimes – Firearms – Penalties and Procedures (Violent Firearms Offender Act of 2023)

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2023RS/bills/hb/hb0952f.pdf)
provenance.note: As filed; first reader, no committee action or passage vote in the record. Quoted parts are abridged from a long bill (also covers machine-gun and assault-weapon use penalties, stolen-firearm possession, ID-mark removal, § 5–144, firearm use as non-'technical violation' of probation/parole in Correctional Services § 6–101). Bail and probation parts apply only to gun crimes, so not treated as separate topics. 'Not less than years' in § 4–204 is as extracted (number lost in text; the bill's own 5-year minimum is in the following sentence).

operative_text:
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4–204): A person may not use a firearm in the commission of a crime of violence, as defined in § 5–101 of the Public Safety Article, or any felony, whether the firearm is operable or inoperable at the time of the crime. A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and, in addition to any other penalty imposed for the crime of violence or felony, shall be sentenced: FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, to imprisonment for not less than years and not exceeding 20 years; AND FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 10 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 7–104): A PERSON CONVICTED OF THEFT OF A FIREARM, INCLUDING AN ANTIQUE FIREARM OR A REPLICA OF AN ANTIQUE FIREARM, IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND: (I) 1. FOR A FIRST CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 2 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $2,500; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 15 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000;
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Procedure § 5–202): A District Court commissioner may not authorize the pretrial release of a defendant charged with A CRIME LISTED IN SUBPARAGRAPH (II) OF THIS PARAGRAPH if the defendant: has previously been convicted of a crime of violence or A CRIME LISTED IN SUBPARAGRAPH (II) OF THIS PARAGRAPH; OR IS ON PRETRIAL RELEASE FOR A CRIME OF VIOLENCE OR A CRIME LISTED IN SUBPARAGRAPH (II) OF THIS PARAGRAPH.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–134): A DEALER OR OTHER PERSON MAY NOT SELL, RENT, LOAN, OR TRANSFER A REGULATED FIREARM TO A PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE IF THE DEALER OR OTHER PERSON HAS ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE THAT THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE: (I) WAS PREVIOUSLY CONVICTED OF: 1. A CRIME OF VIOLENCE; (II) INTENDS TO USE THE REGULATED FIREARM TO: 1. COMMIT A CRIME; OR 2. CAUSE HARM TO THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, TRANSFEREE, OR RECIPIENT OR ANOTHER PERSON. A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 15 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–133): EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SUBSECTION (C) OF THIS SECTION, A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A MISDEMEANOR AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO: 1. FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 5 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–141): A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and on conviction is subject to imprisonment FOR NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS AND not exceeding 15 years AND a fine not exceeding $25,000.
